speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

text: That diagnosis does not fit the clinical picture of free mediastinal air, crepitus, and shock; based on these findings, the diagnosis is ready as Mediastinitis secondary to esophageal perforation.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see the clinical picture clearly now; the combination of forceful vomiting, subcutaneous emphysema (crunching sound), free mediastinal air on X-ray, and hypotension confirms a medical emergency. The patient has a Boerhaave syndrome with resulting mediastinitis and septic shock. Please prepare the patient for immediate surgical intervention and broad-spectrum antibiotics while we obtain blood cultures.
